findings.evidence: Minimum password length is 7, target is 14
findings.risk: Short passwords are vulnerable to brute force and dictionary attacks
findings.recommended_remediation: Set minimum password length to 14 via Default Domain Policy or PSO

findings.risk: Users can set trivially simple passwords like 'password123'
findings.recommended_remediation: Enable password complexity in Default Domain Policy

findings.evidence: Password history count is 0, target is 24
findings.risk: Users can reuse old passwords, defeating rotation goals
findings.recommended_remediation: Set password history to 24 in Default Domain Policy

findings.risk: Brute force attacks against accounts have no rate limit
findings.recommended_remediation: Set lockout threshold to 5 attempts with 30 minute duration

findings.evidence: Account: Administrator, State: Enabled, ServiceAccount: No, PasswordLastSet: 2026-04-16, MemberOf: Group Policy Creator Owners, Domain Admins, Enterprise Admins, Schema Admins, Administrators
findings.risk: Passwords that never expire increase exposure window if compromised
findings.recommended_remediation: Remove PasswordNeverExpires flag, implement managed service accounts or gMSAs where applicable

findings.evidence: Missing audit subcategories: Process Creation, Special Logon, Account Management, Object Access; Sysmon not installed; PowerShell Script Block Logging not enabled
findings.risk: Without comprehensive audit logging, attacker activity will go undetected
findings.recommended_remediation: Configure advanced audit policy via GPO for process creation, special logon, account management, and object access. Deploy Sysmon and enable PowerShell script block logging.

findings.evidence: Service account has interactive logon permission - should be restricted; Never logged on

findings.recommended_remediation: Restrict delegation, remove from privileged groups, convert to gMSA, enforce AES-only Kerberos
